2. ⚙️ System Architecture & Components

2.1 The Layout Engine: timelineLayoutEngine.js

The layout engine is a pure computation function that maps a chronological sequence of events to specific visual grid lanes.

Chronological Sorting: Sorts events from newest to oldest based on their end dates (with ongoing events at the top) and start dates.

Lane Selection Algorithm:
Root events (parent === "main") are greedy; they default to Lane 0 to form a continuous mainline if no other event is occupying it.

Sub-branches check for the first free lane starting at parentLane + 1. This allows parallel events (like DLR research and the Master Project) to run side-by-side on distinct vertical lanes.

Deterministic SHAs: Uses a string-hashing algorithm to generate a stable, 7-character hexadecimal SHA hash for each event.

Coordinate Mapping: Translates table rows to pixel layout constraints (yStart, yEnd, and laneX) so that the SVG commit graph overlays perfectly onto the HTML table.

2.2 The SVG Commit Graph: TimelineGraph.jsx

Gapless Same-Lane Lines: Checks if node.parentLane === node.lane to render lines directly from yStart to yEnd bypassing branching curve offsets. This creates a solid line running through Lane 0.

Bézier Curve Branches: Utilizes cubic Bézier paths (M x1 y1 C ...) to smoothly curve branches off parent lines when starting, and merge them back when terminating.

Interactive Hover States: Highlights active rows, scales up commit dots, and renders pulsing glows behind selected nodes.

2.3 The GitKraken Shell Dashboard: TechnologyPage.jsx

Git Controls Bar: Displays simulated Pull, Push, and Fetch actions. Clicking these prompts loading spinners and confirmation notifications.

Selection History (Undo/Redo): The Undo and Redo buttons act as checkout actions, stepping backwards and forwards through the career commits.

Collapsible Sidebar: A multi-section navigator displaying local branches, remote branches, tags, and stashes. Selecting any item automatically checkout-scrolls to the corresponding timeline entry.

Live Search filter: Text-filtering highlights matching rows and dims non-matching rows to 12% opacity. This preserves the graph visualization while filtering.

Commit Details Panel: Renders commit hashes, parent commits, author signatures, dates, role titles, and simulated file trees.

Interactive Diff Code Viewer: Expanding a file shows a color-coded code diff representing skills used (e.g. C++, Unity C#, Python ROS, Node.js). It includes a copy-to-clipboard button.

3. 🌀 Dynamic Interactive Physics Background

The canvas-based grid background represents a core design element of this portfolio:

3.1 Physics Grid Canvas: TechGraphBackground.jsx

Mesh Construction: Renders a HTML5 canvas-based grid. Major lines are rendered heavier to outline visual zones, and crosshair ticks mark major intersections.

Interactive Physics Mesh: Intersections behave as physical particles controlled by equations:
$$\text{force} = \frac{\text{glowRadius} - \text{distance}}{\text{glowRadius}}$$
$$\text{velocity} \mathrel{+}= \text{direction} \times \text{force} \times \text{gravity}$$

Spring Dynamics: Particles spring back to their original anchors using spring hook constants and friction dampers:
$$\text{acceleration}{\text{spring}} = (\text{anchor} - \text{position}) \times \text{springConstant}$$
$$\text{velocity} \mathrel{+}= \text{acceleration}{\text{spring}}$$
$$\text{velocity} \mathrel{\times}= \text{friction}$$

Mouse Radial Glow: Draws a smooth gradient glow centered around the mouse cursor with adjustable colors and radius.

Ambient Breathing Pulse: Modulates base transparency on a sine wave to make the grid feel alive:
$$\alpha = \alpha_{\text{base}} + \sin(\text{time} \times \text{breathSpeed}) \times \text{breathAmplitude}$$

3.2 Developer Configuration Panel: TechDevPanel.jsx

A floating dashboard controls panel (▸ BG DEV at the bottom left) letting users dynamically tune values at runtime:

Grid Controls: Adjust minor/major grid size spacing, baseline opacity, and base color.

Breath Controls: Enable/disable breathing, adjust speed, and modulate wave amplitude.

Glow Controls: Toggle glow, adjust color, radius, and intensity.

Physics Constants: Tune gravity force, spring coefficient, and friction damping.

This is the heart of the change — a ~230-line canvas component. Here's how it works:

Initialization:

Uses ResizeObserver on the parent container to dynamically resize the canvas
Creates a 2D array of particles (one per grid intersection point)
Each particle stores: original position (ox, oy), current animated position (x, y), velocity (vx, vy), and whether it's on a major grid line
The render loop (requestAnimationFrame):

Every frame:

Read config values (spacing, colors, alpha, physics, toggles)

Smooth-lerp mouse position (15% per frame)

Calculate breath offset: sin(time * breathSpeed) * breathAmplitude

Update glow opacity fade (0→1 when mouse enters, 1→0 when leaves)

For each particle:
If glow enabled & mouse inside: apply gravity force toward cursor

Apply spring force back to original position

Apply friction to velocity

Update position

Draw base mesh (all lines at base alpha + breath offset)

Draw glow mesh pass (radial gradient around cursor position)
Key differences from BrainPageBackground:

Only renders the graph mesh (no dot grid — that's the creative side)
Scoped to container bounds (not full viewport)
Uses ResizeObserver instead of window.resize (works in a flex panel)
